title: Quadratic gate equation
statement: Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits and $g$ gates, and use $1+n+g$ variables over $\mathbb{F}_2$. For a gate $i$, define a homogeneous quadratic equation with right-hand side $0$ as follows, writing $c$ for the constant-coordinate variable, $x_j$ for input variables, and $y_k$ for gate variables: if gate $i$ reads input $j$, its equation is $y_i c+x_j c=0$; if it is the constant $0$, its equation is $y_i c=0$; if it is the constant $1$, its equation is $y_i c+c^2=0$; if it negates an earlier gate $k$, its equation is $y_i c+y_k c+c^2=0$; if it is the conjunction of earlier gates $k$ and $$, its equation is $y_i c+y_k y_\ell=0$; and if it is their disjunction, its equation is $y_i c+y_k c+y_\ell c+y_k y_\ell=0$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits and $g$ gates
The gate at $i$ is one of the listed gate types, with the corresponding input or earlier-gate indices
